newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Islamic militant group claims Jerusalem attack.
newsitem.headline: Islamic militant group claims Jerusalem attack.

text.p: The militant Palestinian Islamic group Hamas claimed responsibility for a double suicide bombing that killed 14 people and wounded more than 150 in a crowded Jerusalem market on Wednesday.

Hamas' military wing issued the claim in a leaflet faxed to an international news agency which gave Israel until 9 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Sunday to free all Palestinian prisoners including ailing Hamas founder Sheikh Ahmed Yassin.
"The Izz el-Deen al-Qassam Brigades martyrs unit for emancipation of prisoners claims responsibility for the jihad (holy struggle) operation in Jerusalem," the leaflet said.
Hamas sources said the suicide attackers came from the West Bank.

They said the group carried out the attack in Jerusalem's main Jewish market to avenge a Jewish woman's pasting of posters depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig on storefronts in the West Bank town of Hebron last month.
The bombings occurred on the eve of the scheduled return to the Middle East of U.S. envoy Dennis Ross in a fresh bid to end a peacemaking crisis over Jewish settlement.
U.S. President Bill Clinton said the visit would be postponed while Israel mourned its dead.

The Hamas sources said the attack also was in retaliation for the publication in an Israeli science magazine of a photomontage of the Virgin Mary with a cow's head. The photo, to illustrate a story on cloning, angered Palestinian Christians.
The leaflet demanded the immediate release of Sheikh Yassin, the Hamas spiritual leader arrested by Israel in May 1989, and all other Palestinian prisoners, including those from Hamas.
"The time to carry out our just demands starts from the date of this leaflet and ends at 9 o'clock on Sunday evening, August 3," it said without elaborating.

It called on the Red Cross, the ambassadors of Egypt and Germany and other international institutions to supervise the release of prisoners. Palestinian sources said there were some 4,000 Arab prisoners in Israeli jails.

"We welcome all efforts of mediation in this framework to achieve our legitimate demands," the statement said. The group's military wing called on Hamas political leaders to "mobilise and conduct necessary contacts" to achieve their demands.

Dr Abdel Aziz Rantisi, a Hamas political leader in the self-ruled Gaza Strip, said he thought the mention of ambassadors and the naming of Hamas officials was "peculiar" and questioned its credibility.
"I feel surprised by such a leaflet, especially when my name is mentioned. Therefore I doubt the credibility of such a leaflet."

Hamas, a militant opponent of Israeli-PLO peace deals, has claimed responsibility for many of the suicide attacks that have rocked the Jewish state since it first signed an interim peace deal with Yasser Arafat's PLO in 1993.
In March, a Hamas bomber killed himself and three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe days after Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Israeli police have arrested and charged a 26-year Jewish woman with pasting the anti-Moslem posters in Hebron.
